name: Necromancer Necrotech
body:
The necrotech is a necromancer with access to advanced technology. They use this new medium to improve upon their minions and enhance their capabilities; bringing macabre new life to the undead they control.

Hit Dice d6.

Charnel Touch (Su)

Necrotechs increase their charnel touch base damage to 2d8 at 12th level. They do not increase it to 3d8.

This alters the progression of charnel touch.

Technomancer Training (Ex)

A necrotech adds Disable Device (Int), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), and Linguistics (Int) to his list of class skills and removes Appraise, Knowledge (dungeoneering), and Sleight of Hand.

At 1st level, necrotechs gain proficiency with all firearms, and they gain Technologist as a bonus feat. At 5th level, he also gains Skill Focus (knowledge [engineering]) as a bonus feat.

This alters the necromancer’s class skills and proficiencies.

Recondition (Su)

At 2nd level, a necrotech can keep a single piece of still-functioning timeworn technology in good working order.

Reconditioning a timeworn technological item takes 8 hours, after which the item no longer has a chance of glitching when used by the necrotech and can be recharged normally by the necrotech but no one else.

Keeping a reconditioned item working requires 1 hour of maintenance each day (this can overlap with other preparations, if any), or the item reverts to a normal piece of timeworn technology and must be reconditioned again. At 4th level and every 3 levels thereafter, a necrotech can keep an additional item in good working order, without increasing his daily maintenance time.

Efficient Construction (Ex)

At 3rd level, a necrotech using a technological crafting lab reduces the necessary energy expenditure of the facility by 25%.

At 10th level, this energy reduction increases to 50%.

This ability replaces cruelty.

Spell Battery (Su)

At 3rd level as a swift action, a necrotech can expend an unused spell slot to power a technological device he touches.

Each spell level expended in this way grants the device 1 charge.

Any charges unused at the end of the round are lost, and any charges used by the device that round that aren’t provided by the necrotech must come from the device’s own power reserves.

He can use this ability to power timeworn technology. He can’t power devices that don’t use charges.

Technical Expertise (Ex)

Starting at 4th level, a necrotech adds his class level to Craft, Disable Device, Knowledge (engineering), and Linguistics checks regarding technology.

This replaces spectral hand.

Command Robot (Sp)

At 5th level, a necrotech can issue a command to a robot within 30 feet as a standard action once per day. The command must be in a language the robot can understand.

Robots can resist this ability by succeeding at a Will saving throw.

DC of 10 + 1/2 the necrotech’s class level + his Charisma

At 8th level, the necrotech can use this ability twice per day, and at 10th level he can use it three times per day.

This ability otherwise functions as suggestion, save that it is not mind-affecting and can only affect constructs with the robot subtype.

Graft Technology (Ex)

Also at 5th level, undead created by a necrotech can each be outfitted with one of the following technological upgrades. The necrotech chooses which option to apply when he creates an undead.

Recognition Display: Grant the undead lifesense, which allows it to detect the presence of living creatures within 60 feet.
Robot Legs: Increase the undead’s movement speed by +10 feet.
Shield Plating: Increase the undead’s natural armor bonus by +2.
Targeting Sensor: Grant the undead a +1 enhancement bonus on attacks and damage. If the necromancer has a weapon in his possession with a higher enhancement bonus, he can grant that bonus to exactly one of the undead.
Recycle Technology (Ex)

At 4th level, a necrotech can dismantle existing technological items and construct new ones from the parts, though such creations are prone to malfunctioning. He trades in each item for an amount of crafting potential based on a fraction of its crafting cost (not price), as described below. He can use this potential and his technological crafting feats to make a new item. For example, a necrotech could use a broken laser pistol in place of 500 gp for crafting technological items (10% of the laser pistol‘s crafting cost of 5,000 gp). He then follows the normal rules for crafting a technological item (see page 16), except that he must pay at least 50% of the crafting cost using recycled technology. If he pays 100% of the cost in this fashion, he crafts the item at double the normal speed. In the process of cannibalizing the old items, the new items are destroyed and any excess gold value is lost.

The item he creates is considered timeworn technology, even if new items were broken down to build it. Recycle technology cannot be used to build constructs, cybertech, pharmaceuticals, or technology that uses nanites.

Technology Status	Crafting Potential
Fully functioning	100% of crafting cost
Reconditioned	75% of crafting cost
Timeworn technology	50% of crafting cost
Broken or nonfunctional	10% of crating cost
Applied Learning (Ex)

At 9th level, when a necrotech succeeds at a saving throw against a technological effect that has reduced effects on a successful save, he instead avoids the effect entirely. A helpless or flat-footed necrotech does not benefit from this ability.

Technic Spell Mastery (Ex)

At 9th level, a necrotech selects one of the following spells: antitech field, destroy robot, detect radiation, discharge, greater discharge, greater remove radioactivity, infuse robot, irradiate, magic circle against technology, memory of function, rebuke technology, recharge, remove radioactivity, protection from technology, or technomancy.

If the spell chosen isn’t one that’s normally on his necromancer spell list, he adds it to his class spell list at the level a wizard casts the spell. The spell chosen must be of a spell level he would otherwise be able to cast. If he prepares spells, he can prepare this spell one additional time in excess of the normal maximum number of spells he can prepare. If he casts spells spontaneously, he adds the spell to his spells known, and can cast this spell once per day without using a daily spell slot.

At 5th level, he picks another spell from the list above, and at 8th level, he picks a 3rd spell from the list above.

Unified Energy (Su)

At 11th level, a necrotech can draw power from a technological device in his possession to cast a spell he knows without expending a spell slot. He consumes 2 charges from the device for each spell level of the spell being cast.

In the process of casting the spell, he can apply any of his metamagic feats, using a number of charges appropriate to the increase in spell level, but he cannot exceed the highest effective level of spell he is able to cast.

The necrotech can use this ability multiple times per day, but never in excess of a number of charges equal to his necromancer level.

Fortification (Ex)

A necrotech doesn’t gain light fortification until 13th level.

He still gains moderate fortification at 17th level, and heavy fortification at 20th level.

This alters the progression of fortification.

Field Improvisation (Ex)

At 10th level, a necrotech can recycle technology with astounding speed. Each hour of crafting when using his recycle technology ability is equivalent to 8 hours of uninterrupted crafting. He can perform up to 8 hours of such amazingly efficient work per day.

Any item the necrotech completes is treated as reconditioned for the remainder of that day, even if he has no remaining slots.

It can also be added permanently to his group of reconditioned items if he has an available slot or stops maintaining one of his current reconditioned items.
